A diameter splits the circle into two halves. The first cut produces 2 pieces. The second cut, also a diameter, crosses the first at the center, dividing each of the 2 pieces into 2, yielding 4. The third cut crosses the previous two at the center, passing through exactly 2 of the existing 4 pieces, dividing them into 2 each, yielding 6. The fourth cut crosses the previous three at the center, passing through exactly 2 of the existing 6 pieces, dividing them into 2 each, yielding 8. In general, the n-th cut adds exactly 2 new pieces because it only passes through 2 regions (one on each side of the center). Total = 2 + (4-1)*2 = 8.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
